subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan (FinServCorp)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan (FinServCorp)

Hi Alice / Tom —

Great to meet you both on the call today. Quick recap and a proposed 6-week POC plan so we can lock scope and owners. Please review and let me know if anything needs to change.

Demo recap (high level)
- Showed Redwood hosted API + demo app: prompt routing, latency/cost tradeoffs, live tracing
- Key value to FinServ: predictable inference latency for low-latency fraud checks, per-route cost visibility, private deployment options for regulated flows

Proposed POC objectives (success criteria)
1) Latency: 95th percentile E2E latency < 250ms for 1k qps synthetic baseline (sampled production traffic)
2) Quality: >= 90% parity on labeled fraud detection prompts vs current model (sample set of 1k prompts)
3) Cost: unit inference cost < $0.008 per call at production-like batching profile
4) Reliability: sustained throughput with no more than 2% error rate over 1-hour sustained run

POC plan (recommended, 6 weeks)
- Week 0 (prep): data & access exchange, target prompt set, instrumentation checklist (1 week)
- Week 1-2 (sandbox): deploy the evaluation model on Redwood hosted sandbox, run scale tests, collect latency/cost metrics
- Week 3-4 (iterative tuning): batching/quantization suggestions, measure quality/regression on labeled set
- Week 5-6 (production simulation): run production-like traffic, handoff to FinServ ops, final report and rollout recommendation

Ownership
- FinServ: Alice Zhang (POC lead), Tom Walker (infra/ops)
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (Eng + success), Rishi Malhotra (solution architecture)

Next steps
1) Confirm success criteria and owners (reply-all)
2) Kickoff call — propose Wed July 21 at 10:00am PT (or suggest alternatives)
3) Share access / sample prompt set and SOC2 link (we'll provide our SOC2 cert and ask for your security questionnaire)

Attachment: finserv_poc_scope.pdf (POC scope & milestones)

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Solutions + Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0147
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@finservcorp.com>

Cc: Tom Walker <tom.walker@finservcorp.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC plan (FinServCorp)

Thanks Marissa — really helpful write-up and love the structure. A few small edits from our side:

- Success criteria: on latency, can we set 95th <= 250ms (agree) but also add 99th <= 400ms as a guardrail for tail behavior
- Quality: we'll measure parity on a labeled set but will also require a manual review on a 200-sample subset for false positives
- Cost: the target looks reasonable, we'll validate against our budget once we have initial numbers

Owners are correct. Tom and I can lead instrumentation on our side; he's looped in. We can do the kickoff Wed July 21 at 10am PT.

One question: during sandbox runs do you recommend starting on Hosted or should we plan for a Dedicated instance from day 1 for more consistent measurements?

I'll attach our security questionnaire (separate email) — Tom will follow up with any infra-level details we need to share.

Best,
Alice
Alice Zhang | Head of ML Engineering
FinServCorp

Thanks Alice — great feedback, and happy to add the 99th percentile tail guardrail + the manual review step to the plan.

Recommendation on capacity: start on Hosted sandbox for speed of onboarding and to get baseline latency/cost numbers. If you see high variance in results or need network isolation, we can spin up a Dedicated pool for the production-simulation phase (Week 5-6). We'll document both approaches in the kickoff deck.

I also moved the kickoff to Wed July 21 10:00am PT (confirmed) and added a short agenda: 1) Introductions & scope, 2) Access checklist, 3) Timeline & milestones, 4) Next steps & owners.
